headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty fell for a sixth straight week as crude oil prices crossed $100.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Crude oil prices surged above $100 per barrel due to fears of Saudi Arabian export disruptions.
Geopolitical tensions escalated following Saudi air raid warnings and North Korea's irreversible nuclear status declaration.
Internal corporate governance struggles and a fight for control at Tata Sons dampened investor confidence.
Persistent concerns regarding the US Federal Reserve's interest rate trajectory led to a sixth consecutive weekly decline.
whatHappening: The Nifty 50 is testing a critical support level at 23,050 following a period of sustained selling pressure.
Maruti Suzuki has launched its S-CNG range as part of a strategic goal to sell 1 million green vehicles.
Goldman Sachs has identified HFCL and Polycab India as key companies enabling the growth of AI technology.
Global energy markets are on high alert as Houthi attacks intensify, threatening major oil supply routes.

summary:
Indian markets extended their losing streak to six weeks as global energy shocks and geopolitical instability weighed on sentiment.
Surging crude oil prices above $100 and internal leadership conflicts within the Tata Group have heightened volatility across major sectors.
Investors are now closely monitoring the 23,050 Nifty support level and specific growth themes like AI enablers and green energy.
